/-!
# Erdős Problem 1206

*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/1206](https://www.erdosproblems.com/1206)
- [Er80] Erdős, Paul, *A survey of problems in combinatorial number theory*. Ann. Discrete Math.
  (1980), 89-115.
- [GGK26] M. Garaev, F. Garayev, and S. Konyagin, *On Sidon sets with squares, cubes, and quartics
  in short intervals*. arXiv:2602.08807 (2026).
- [GaKo24] Gabdullin, M. R. and Konyagin, S. V., *Trigonometric polynomials with frequencies in the
  set of cubes*. Math. Notes (2024), 336--340.
-/

@[expose] public section

namespace Erdos1206

/--
Does $\{1,2^3,\ldots,N^3\}$ contain a Sidon set of size $\gg N$?
-/
@[category research open, AMS 5 11]
theorem erdos_1206.parts.i : answer(sorry) ↔
    ∃ c : ℝ, 0 < c ∧ ∀ᶠ N in Filter.atTop, ∃ S : Finset ℕ,
      S ⊆ (Finset.Icc 1 N).image (fun n => n ^ 3) ∧
      IsSidon (S : Set ℕ) ∧ c * (N : ℝ) ≤ (S.card : ℝ) := by
  sorry

/--
Is there an infinite set $A\subset \mathbb{N}$ of positive density such that $\{a^3 : a\in A\}$ is a Sidon set?
-/
@[category research open, AMS 5 11]
theorem erdos_1206.parts.ii : answer(sorry) ↔
    ∃ A : Set ℕ, A.Infinite ∧ 0 < A.lowerDensity ∧
      IsSidon ((fun a : ℕ => a ^ 3) '' A) := by
  sorry

end Erdos1206

reformulations.difference: Lean uses a set with positive lower density, whereas the original source [Er80, p. 109] asks for an increasing sequence satisfying a_i < C i whose cube sums are distinct.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: If a_i < C i, its range has at least floor(N/C) elements up to N, giving positive lower density. Conversely, positive lower density gives an eventual bound |A ∩ [1,N]| ≥ cN for some c > 0. Increasingly enumerating A, after deleting 0 if necessary, yields a_i = O(i); enlarging the constant handles the finite initial segment and makes a_i < C i strict. Deleting 0 preserves lower density and the Sidon property. Thus the Lean condition captures Erdős’s explicit linear-growth question. This argument does not identify positive lower density with existence of a natural-density limit. The lower-density/counting-function equivalence and redundancy of A.Infinite were proved in the scratch file, but the full sequence reformulation was not formalized.

review.notes: Both declarations were checked; no mathematical defect was found. Part i correctly places a uniform positive constant before the eventual quantifier and allows the finite Sidon subset to depend on N. Scratch experiments in /workspace/review/scratch.lean compile successfully: they verify cube injectivity, image cardinality N, density boundary cases, positive lower density implying infinitude, and equivalence with an eventual linear counting bound. Finite tests cover N = 0 through 15 and detect the expected 1729 collision at N = 12. Live erdosproblems.com requests were blocked by Cloudflare, so the complete archived problem page and original survey were used; the current public database corroborates the open status. For Gabdullin–Konyagin, the publisher abstract was accessible but the full article was paywalled.
